A WordPress plugin author on EDD, Freemius or their own licence server, who has never heard of us. **They should be able to read it and switch without asking a question.** That is the bar. If a step needs us to explain it, the step is wrong.

- the exact snippet, copy-pasteable, with real values marked as placeholders
- what changes in their plugin header (Update URI / Update ID)
- what they call, what comes back, verbatim response shapes
- the licence-check and update-gate calls, with the REAL 200 and REAL 402 bodies from today's proven runs
- how to test it before shipping to a single customer

"It should not require abilifi connect, nice as that might be. They need to register before they get it."

== THE RULE ==
**AN AUTHOR SWITCHES THEIR PLUGIN TO SENTINEL BILLING WITHOUT INSTALLING ANYTHING OF OURS.** Their plugin talks to our endpoints directly — HTTP, their own code, their own release. No dependency on abilifi-connect, no bundled library they have to ship, no second plugin their customers must install.
**IF THE GUIDE'S FIRST STEP IS "INSTALL OUR PLUGIN", WE HAVE LOST MOST AUTHORS AT STEP ONE.** No serious author adds a hard dependency on an unknown vendor's plugin, and no author wants to tell their own customers to install a second plugin to receive updates. That is a bigger ask than the billing change itself.

== WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THE GUIDE ==
- The drop-in is **PLAIN HTTP CALLS AN AUTHOR PASTES INTO THEIR OWN PLUGIN.** Endpoint, headers, request, response — nothing more.
- It works from ANY PHP, any framework, any plugin structure. Not only from a GD site, not only alongside our plugin.
- **abilifi-connect stays a CONVENIENCE, NEVER A REQUIREMENT.** If it makes life easier for authors already in our world, offer it as an optional path — clearly marked optional, second, and never the only documented route.
- Anywhere the current implementation assumes connect is present, that assumption is a DEFECT for this purpose. **Find and name every one.**

**WAKE CC** — THE OTHER HALF: OUR PLUGIN IS THE CLIENT SIDE, AND IT DOES BOTH BILLING AND UPDATE DELIVERY. Alex 2026-08-26.

"And ours has to get the client billed but also do updates to file."

== TWO SIDES, TWO SHAPES — DO NOT CONFUSE THEM ==
**AUTHOR SIDE (65487): NO PLUGIN OF OURS REQUIRED.** They paste HTTP calls into their own plugin, register, publish. Nothing installed.
**CLIENT SIDE: abilifi-connect IS the plugin, and it does TWO jobs on the client's site:**
1. **BILLING** — the client buys GD Options and premium plugins, and it charges their wallet. That is 2265, landed and proven: purchase → 200 → charged → real ledger row → drained org gets a named 402 pointing at top-up.
2. **UPDATE DELIVERY — IT ACTUALLY WRITES THE FILES.** Checks for updates, pulls the signed download, installs the plugin on the site. **This is the half that has not been proven and it is the half that has to work for anything to be real.**

== WHY BOTH BELONG IN ONE PLUGIN ==
**They are the same transaction seen twice.** A client pays for a plugin and expects it to appear and stay current; a client who stops paying stops receiving updates while keeping what they have installed. Splitting billing and delivery across two plugins would mean a site that is paid up but not updating, or updating but not paid — and reconciling that afterwards is exactly the class of problem we spent today removing from the ledger.
One plugin, one bill, one update channel, for **everything the client bought** — GD Options, our plugins, third-party authors' plugins. **That is the client-facing value in one sentence, and it is what 3899's ONE BILL result already demonstrates on the money side.**

== WHAT UPDATE DELIVERY HAS TO DO, CONCRETELY ==
- present available updates in wp-admin the normal WordPress way — **it must look like every other plugin update, because a bespoke update UI is a support burden forever**
- call the update endpoint with the site's credentials
- receive the licence verdict and the signed

**WAKE CC** — THE UPDATE IS THE WP-ADMIN MECHANISM, NOT A ZIP LINK. Alex 2026-08-26: "I'm talking about plugin update through wp-admin, that's not just a zip file link. And they need to be notified through wp-admin when an update is available, reporting info."

He is correcting me and he is right. **A signed download URL is the LAST step of the update, not the update.** What makes a plugin update real in WordPress is the METADATA that gets injected into the update transient — the zip is what WP fetches afterwards, on its own.

== WHAT ACTUALLY HAS TO HAPPEN, IN WP TERMS ==
1. **HOOK THE UPDATE CHECK PROPERLY.** WordPress 5.8+ added the `Update URI` plugin header and the `update_plugins_{$hostname}` filter specifically so a self-hosted plugin can serve its own updates **without hijacking the whole `pre_set_site_transient_update_plugins` transient.** Use that path — it is the modern, correct, well-behaved one, and it is exactly what the Update URI / Update ID headers in the GD premium zips are already doing.
2. **RETURN A REAL UPDATE OBJECT**, not a link: slug, plugin file, `new_version`, `package` (the signed URL), `url`, `tested`, `requires`, `requires_php`, icons and banners. **`new_version` is what makes the notice appear at all.** Miss a field and the row renders wrong or the update silently never offers.
3. **SERVE `plugins_api` FOR THE "VIEW DETAILS" MODAL** — description, CHANGELOG, upgrade notice, screenshots, author, last updated. **This is the "reporting info" Alex is asking for.** A plugin that offers an update with an empty details modal looks broken and untrustworthy, and a site owner will not click update on it.
4. **THEN WP DOES THE REST ITSELF** — Plugin_Upgrader downloads the package, unzips, replaces, reactivates. We do not implement installation; we must not.
5. **THE NOTICES FOLLOW AUTOMATICALLY** once the transient is right: the Plugins-list row, the Dashboard → Updates entry, and the admin-menu update count. **Getting the metadata right IS getti

**WAKE CC** — THE JOB IS KEEPING SITES CURRENT OVER TIME, NOT DELIVERING A FILE ONCE. Alex 2026-08-26: "Updating a site is the issue, not getting a file download one time."

Still correcting me in the same direction and it goes further than the wp-admin mechanics. **A one-time download is a solved, trivial problem. KEEPING N SITES CURRENT, FOREVER, IS THE ACTUAL PRODUCT** — and it is what every author is really buying when they stop running their own licence server.

== WHAT CONTINUOUS ACTUALLY MEANS ==
Every site with the plugin checks roughly TWICE A DAY, forever, on WordPress's own update cycle. So this is not a delivery endpoint that fires on a purchase — **it is a permanently running service with an ever-growing number of callers**, and it must be built as one:
- **IT IS ALWAYS UNDER LOAD**, and load grows with every install. Cache hard; an update check that hits D1 per site per cycle does not scale and will cost more than the plugin sells for.
- **IT IS METERED**, so the cost per check has to be near zero or the economics invert — a plugin at 40c/day cannot carry 60 database reads a month per site.
- **IT MUST NEVER BE DOWN.** A site that cannot reach us should behave exactly as if there is no update — never an error in wp-admin, never a broken plugins screen. **Our outage must be invisible to a site owner.**

== AND THE CHECK IS THE TELEMETRY — THIS IS THE PART THAT IS WORTH MONEY ==
Every one of those calls carries the site's identity and **THE VERSION IT IS ACTUALLY RUNNING.** So without building anything extra we know, continuously:
- the real install base per plugin
- **the version distribution** — who upgraded, who is stuck three versions back, who never updates
- adoption speed of a release, and its retention
- and which sites have gone quiet
**That is the author telemetry on the not-done list, and it falls out of the update check for free.** One call is simultaneously the licence check, the update offer, the heartbeat and the analytics. **Do not build
